column1: # Targets of tools/wasm-perf/tests/bench.sh: the Lean tool's minimum CPU time (user+system,
# seconds, over the runs) and maximum resident memory (MB) per case and input. Set on
# 2026-11-09 (i7-8700, 12 threads, load 5-8 from concurrent builds) at about 3x the measured
# value after the round's optimisations, so that load does not trip them while a regression to
# the previous behaviour (e.g. jco-new 5 s on xf400, wit-print 3 s and 420 MB, wit-parse a
# stack overflow on xf1200, wac-compose 690 MB on xf1200) does. The smallest inputs are
# dominated by start-up (about 75 MB, 0.05 s: the executables are 145 MB).
# an earlier step (perf): the jco-new and jco-validate rows lowered to about 3x the values after
# Perf.JcoMain/ValidateF/XEncodeB and the decoder leaves (jco-new xf400 0.71 s 168 MB, xf1200
# 1.96 s 322 MB; jco-validate xf400 0.62 s, xf1200 1.62 s); the callsN rows guard against a
# validator quadratic in the number of functions (calls20k took 31.6 s to validate before).
# an earlier step (perf): jco rows lowered after Perf.ValidateR (reversed-stack validator) and the
# single input decode of wasm-jco new (jco-new xf400 1.09 s 163 MB, xf1200 1.93 s 312 MB under
# load 25); wit-parse RSS rows lowered after Perf.WatReadB (byte lexer: xf1200 438 MB, was 675).
